clue.text: Charlie more than 400m behind given a hand

parts.note: a running track lap is 400 metres, so a runner more than that behind has been lapped

explanation.surface: A runner called Charlie trails the field by over a lap yet still gets applause.
explanation.walkthrough: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet; 400m is one lap of a standard athletics track.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given a hand is to receive applause, which is to be clapped by an audience.

clue.text: Party politician supports more or less

indicators.note: in a down clue the politician sits beneath, supporting the other piece

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means approximately

explanation.surface: A political party gets roughly the backing of an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a faction or group sharing a cause, as in the opposing camp.

clue.text: Prompter, if traffic jam reported?

indicators.note: signals the sound of the phrase, not its spelling

parts.note: an auto queue, a queue of cars

explanation.surface: A prompter wonders whether a traffic jam has been reported.
explanation.definitionFit: An Autocue is the screen device that shows presenters their script, a mechanical prompter.

clue.text: Ireland starts to rack points up, coming first

indicators.note: in a down clue, the whole is read upwards, so reversed
the starting letters of rack and points

parts.note: the first letters of rack and points

explanation.surface: Ireland begins racking up points and takes the lead in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier, preceding in time or order.

clue.text: Threshold cats, dogs, etc cross over

indicators.note: the combined pieces are turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross, especially in a church

explanation.surface: Cats and dogs crossing the threshold of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep is the step at the entrance of a house, the literal threshold.

clue.text: Charlie's face smiles having taken lead in race

definitions.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool

parts.note: mug is slang for a person's face

indicators.note: the letter is taken away from the word for smiles
the lead, or first letter, in the word race

parts.note: its first letter is the lead

explanation.surface: Charlie's grinning face as he takes the lead in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie looked like a name to start the wordplay, but here it is the definition: a charlie, like a muggins, is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a gullible person or idiot who gets taken advantage of.

clue.text: Uncertainties PM ideally brought to an early conclusion

parts.note: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister

indicators.note: the word is ended early, losing its last letter

parts.note: best is how things would ideally go

explanation.surface: A prime minister's uncertain plans are ideally cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybes are possibilities not yet settled, things that remain doubtful.

clue.text: In storm, commercial vehicle is waterproof

definitions.note: used as a verb, to make something proof against water

indicators.note: the van and is go in the storm

parts.note: a van is a commercial vehicle

explanation.surface: A delivery van in a storm proves to be watertight.
explanation.definitionFit: To galvanise is to coat metal with zinc, protecting it from rust caused by water.

clue.text: Boxer punches popular 5D without good reason

indicators.note: the boxer punches into the pair of letters

parts.note: read literally, V is Roman five followed by D

explanation.surface: A boxer punching for no reason, with a cross-reference to 5 Down.
explanation.walkthrough: 5D looks like a reference to the clue at 5 Down; it is just Roman five and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Invalid describes an argument or claim lacking a sound basis.

clue.text: Calm bully teased by head

definitions.note: a noun here, as in a state of calm

indicators.note: to bully is to push around, so the letters are pushed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A calm bully is teased by the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Head looks like a headteacher; it is a headland, a ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedateness is composure, a quiet and unhurried manner.

clue.text: Apron worn in companionable relationship

indicators.note: the edge-and-worn pieces go in the word for companionable

parts.note: maty, or matey, means friendly and companionable
an apron can be an edge or border, as on a stage, so a rim

explanation.surface: Wearing an apron as part of a cosy domestic partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: Maty is an accepted variant spelling of matey.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrimony is the state of marriage, the most formal kind of personal union between two people.

clue.text: Very cross, if cover lets four or six through?

indicators.note: the cover lets something pass, so it admits the numeral
the numeral passes through into the middle of the cover

parts.note: Roman four is IV and six is VI, and either one placed in the cover gives the same answer

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at cover lets a boundary through, enraging the bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is also a cricket fielding position, and four or six are boundary scores, which explains the question mark. IV or VI both fit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid is an intensifying word for being furiously angry.

clue.text: Troupe putting daughter in best role, clap wildly

indicators.note: putting one piece into another signals insertion
says where the letter is put
the letters of best role and clap are thrown into a wild new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters for the mix
taken as written, letters for the mix

explanation.surface: A dance troupe gives a daughter the best role and the audience claps wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: The corps de ballet is the ensemble of dancers in a ballet company, a troupe performing together.

clue.text: Dance practice, boring kit

explanation.surface: Dance practice treated as dull equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist drill is a bit with spiral grooves used for boring holes, kit for drilling.

clue.text: Very unhappy with journalist penning gag

indicators.note: a pen encloses, so with-and-journalist enclose the word for gag

parts.note: ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable that a journalist has written a joke at their expense.
explanation.walkthrough: Gag looks like a joke being penned, but it means retch.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched describes a person in deep misery or distress.

clue.text: Military leader given a second scar

parts.note: a trice is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A commander given a second scar in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicatrice is a formal or medical word for the mark left by a healed wound.

clue.text: Dungheap in the centre of animal's lair

parts.note: a den is a wild animal's lair

explanation.surface: A pile of dung sits in the middle of a creature's lair.
explanation.definitionFit: A midden is an old word for a refuse heap or dunghill, often studied by archaeologists.

clue.text: Film star catches first wave

indicators.note: the star catches the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a perm is a hair wave
A, as in A1, the first

explanation.surface: A film star catches the first wave of fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Superman is the 1978 film starring Christopher Reeve, the title of a movie.

clue.text: Really marvellous blankets back in hotel providing comfort

indicators.note: the words for really marvellous cover the letter like blankets

parts.note: so, as in so good, means really

indicators.note: the back, or last letter, in the word hotel

parts.note: its last letter is the back

explanation.surface: Fine hotel bedding gives guests comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation, the comfort offered in time of grief.

clue.text: Cut keeping women's charity on reduced income

indicators.note: the word for cut keeps the letter inside

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women, as on lavatory doors

explanation.surface: Funding cuts at a women's charity leave staff earning less.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-paid describes workers who receive poor wages, so their earnings are small.

clue.text: Club you heard evacuated urinals after opening

indicators.note: the emptied word comes after the opening
points to how the word sounds

parts.note: in Italian the club's opening syllable is said like the English word you

indicators.note: the inside letters are emptied out, leaving only the outer two

parts.note: only its first and last letters remain once emptied

explanation.surface: A lavatorial picture of urinals being emptied out after the doors open at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Italians pronounce the J as a Y, so the start of the name sounds like you.
explanation.definitionFit: Juventus is a famous Italian football club based in Turin.

clue.text: Short show Kate adapted is a classic

indicators.note: the letters are adapted, rearranged
the word show is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A short TV show adapted by Kate becomes a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a flat horse race at Epsom, one of the five English Classics.
explanation.definitionFit: In British racing, the Classics are five major races for three-year-olds, and the Oaks is the fillies' race at Epsom.

clue.text: Importance of fact to America?

parts.note: a stat, or statistic, is a fact

explanation.surface: Asking how important a fact is to America.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is standing or prestige, the degree of significance something holds.

clue.text: Unhappy child, heir we spoiled as long as possible

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the letters of heir we are spoiled, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A miserable child and the heir have been spoiled rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down to the wire is an idiom from racing for lasting until the very last moment.

clue.text: One celibate woman beds fellow as a joke

indicators.note: the nun takes the fellow into her, as into a bed

parts.note: a nun takes a vow of celibacy

explanation.surface: A celibate woman sleeps with a man, but only in jest.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something in fun means it is meant playfully, not seriously.

clue.text: Stand and deliver

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tolerate, as in can't stand it

explanation.walkthrough: Stand and deliver is a highwayman's demand, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both enduring something and producing offspring.

clue.text: Two cups affect the quality of porcelain

indicators.note: to cup is to hold within curved hands, so the pair holds the other word

parts.note: to mar is to spoil, affecting quality

explanation.surface: A pair of teacups that lowers the standard of a china set.
explanation.walkthrough: Cups is a verb here, not the crockery it seems to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is a style of Japanese export porcelain decorated in blue, red and gold.

clue.text: Back issue celebrity holds close to her window

indicators.note: the word for issue is read backwards
the word for celebrity holds the letter inside
the close, or last letter, of the word her

parts.note: its last letter is the close

explanation.surface: A back issue of a magazine with a celebrity feature on her.
explanation.definitionFit: A window of opportunity is a limited period, just as a timeframe is a span of time allowed for something.

clue.text: Boy initially seen blushing about short cuts taken in game

indicators.note: the pair of pieces turns about, read backwards
only the first letter of seen is used

explanation.surface: A boy caught blushing after cutting corners in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Short cuts looks like trimming letters, but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In snakes and ladders, a board game, the ladders let a player skip ahead as shortcuts up the board.

clue.text: New queen accepts burden — no trips for her?

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for a person who takes no drug trips

indicators.note: the outer pair takes the burden into it

explanation.surface: A new queen takes on royal duties and so can no longer travel.
explanation.walkthrough: Trips suggests royal travel, but here means drug trips.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-user is someone who does not take drugs, so has no hallucinatory experiences.
